covers.quote: Spell out ordinal numbers from ‘first’ to ‘ninth’. Use numerals for ordinals from ‘10th’ onwards.
Use numerals, not words, when writing ordinals with centuries. This is an exception to the general rule to spell out ‘first’ to ‘ninth’ for ordinals.
Very large ordinals
People find very large rounded numbers easier to read in words rather than numerals. This also applies to ordinal numbers. Spell out the number and include the relevant suffix.
In reference lists, use numerals with a suffix for editions of a publication. This is an exception to the rule to use words for ordinal numbers up to ninth.
If an organisation’s name includes a numeral, write the name as the organisation does. This is an exception to the rule to use words for ordinal numbers up to ninth.

rules.quote: Use words for ordinals up to ‘ninth’ and numerals for ‘10th’ and above
rules.specification: Apply the century, publication-edition, organisation-name and very-large-rounded-number cases as overrides of the general word-versus-numeral rule. rules.violation_condition: An ordinal from first to ninth is written as a numeral, or an ordinal from tenth onwards is written in words, contrary to the applicable general rule or exception.
when: Normally, spell out first to ninth and use numerals from 10th onwards.
Use numerals for ordinals with centuries, including 1st to 9th.
In reference lists, use numerals for publication editions, including editions below 10th.

Dates and regnal numbers have separate rules and are not ordinary ordinal expressions for this check.

Always use numbered lists rather than ordinals when you’re expressing a series of items or steps – for example, in recommendations or instructions.

Ordinals, such as ‘firstly’ and ‘secondly’, are sometimes used in content written for government publications such as journals and reports. In this type of content, they order thoughts without interrupting the flow of the text.

parts.quote: To apply for the grant:
complete the eligibility checklist
submit a business case
provide supporting documents.
If you want to apply for the grant, first complete the eligibility checklist. Second, you must submit a business case; and third, you must provide supporting documents.

rules.quote: Don’t use ordinals to order points in general content.
rules.specification: Treat this as a restriction on ordinal discourse sequencers, not on descriptions of ordinal position such as ‘the first item’. General content may be reworded to remove the sequencing; for a series of items or steps, the page explicitly requires numbered lists.
rules.violation_condition: Running prose uses ordinal expressions to sequence points, items or steps where the content should instead be reworded or presented as a numbered list.
when: Applies to ordering points in general content.
For a series of items or steps, such as recommendations or instructions, the numbered-list alternative is mandatory.
Journal-style content and other government publications may use ordinals to order thoughts without interrupting the flow, subject to the separate pairing and ‘thirdly’ rules.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the general-content restriction, stricter procedural case and publication exception together; G-4 absorbs the heading and alternative formulations.

rules.why: G-2 treats the two reciprocal missing-partner cases as one check; E-2 attaches the contrast pair to the nearby pairing instruction.
